text: In its classical (Cartesian) form, foundationalism demands that basic beliefs be certain, that is, indubitable, incorrigible, and ___ (such that, if the subject is in the relevant state, the belief cannot be false).
explanation: Classical foundationalism (Descartes and the early empiricists) required the foundations to be infallible: being in the relevant mental state guarantees the truth of the basic belief. Modest foundationalism later dropped this demand, allowing basic beliefs to be merely prima facie justified and defeasible.
